name: Typo & Error Pattern
description: Analyzes the presence, frequency, and specific nature of typographical and grammatical errors. Large Language Models operate on token probabilities; they mathematically construct words and sentences, meaning they virtually never make physiological 'keyboard slips' (e.g., 'teh' instead of 'the', transposed adjacent letters) or common cognitive spelling mistakes. When AI does err, it typically produces hallucinated words or unnatural phrasing rather than mechanical typos. Conversely, authentic human writing—even when edited—often retains characteristic micro-errors, homophone confusions ('their'/'there'), or punctuation inconsistencies.
mechanism: The algorithm scans the text against a comprehensive dictionary and a database of common human typographical errors. It classifies detected anomalies into physiological errors (keyboard slips), cognitive errors (phonetic misspellings, homophones), and tokenization artifacts. A completely pristine text devoid of any orthographic imperfections, or one where the only anomalies are bizarre token combinations rather than standard human typos, strongly correlates with machine generation. The presence of authentic, character-level human typos significantly lowers the AI probability score.
useCase: Crucial for analyzing casual text, forum posts, student essays, and social media content where pristine, error-free orthography is highly unnatural for a human author.
strengths:
• Highly reliable negative indicator for AI: the presence of genuine physiological typos (like adjacent keyboard letter swaps) is extremely strong evidence of human authorship.
• Effectively highlights the 'uncanny valley' of over-polished, perfectly spelled LLM outputs.
limitations:
• Easily defeated if a user intentionally inserts typos into AI-generated text or runs it through a 'humanizer' script.
• Less useful on professionally edited, published, or proofread texts (like journalism or academic papers) where humans also achieve near-perfect orthography.
parameters:
Analysis: Dictionary Validation & Error Classification
Metric: Density of Physiological vs. Cognitive Typographical Errors
Output: 0-100 Orthographic Perfection Score
accuracy: Moderate — 65-80% accuracy. Excellent as a secondary feature; it serves primarily to exonerate human writers rather than definitively prove AI generation.

references.title: Jawahar, G. et al. (2020). Automatic Detection of Machine Generated Text: A Critical Survey. COLING.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
